document.title: Clinical accuracy report - iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer

products.name: iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer

tests.item: 临床准确性与重复性验证
tests.condition: 温度23±2℃，湿度55±10%；被试者总数不少于90人，分三组（0-12月婴儿、1-5岁儿童、5岁以上成人），每组发烧与非发烧人数接近
tests.pass_criteria: t检验p>0.05，即DUT与口腔参考温度无显著差异

semantic_fragments.content: Contraindications: It is not recommended for people whose forehead has local lesions, such as inflammation, trauma, recent surgery, etc..

Intended use: The Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is intended for the intermittent measurement of body temperature from the forehead skin surface on people of all ages. It can be used by consumers in the household environment and by healthcare providers.

Device description: The iHealth PT9L Infrared No-Touch Forehead Thermometer is hand-held, reusable, battery operated device, which can measure human body temperature on the skin temperature on one's forehead. Its operation is based on measuring the natural thermal radiation from the central forehead. Put the probe of the thermometer is onto the skin of a patient's central forehead. Pressing the activation button to start the measurement of proposed infrared radiation. The electrical signal read out from the detector is fed to the circuit for amplification and calculation. The final measured temperature will be appeared on a LCD display.

Test method: Step1: Sequence the Participants and sign Serial numbers. Step2: Verify reference thermometer accuracy using water bath. Step3: Supervisor takes DUT and prepares measurement. Step4: Perform three consecutive measurements with time interval no more than 1 min, record results. Step5: Take one RCT oral temperature measurement, record results. Step6: Repeat for all participants (odd-numbered: DUT first then RCT; even-numbered: RCT first then DUT). Final step: Verify reference thermometer accuracy again with water bath.

Subject participation criteria: Total number no less than 90. Within each age group both afebrile and febrile subjects represented by nearly equal numbers. Oral temperature 37.5℃ or higher considered febrile. Group 1: infants 0-12 months, no less than 30. Group 2: children 1-5 years, no less than 30. Group 3: adults older than 5 years, no less than 30. Exclusion: subjects with medical conditions affecting accuracy (e.g., inflammation at measuring site), subjects who took antipyretics in preceding 120 min.

Subject distribution results: Group1(Infants): 40 participants (F=18, M=22, Febrile=16, Afebrile=24); Group2(Children): 40 participants (F=22, M=18, Febrile=15, Afebrile=25); Group3(Adults): 50 participants (F=26, M=24, Febrile=20, Afebrile=30); Total: 130 participants (Female=66/50.8%, Male=64/49.2%, Febrile=51/39.2%, Afebrile=79/60.8%).
